title: DOCKMIND: bounded six-parameter fit of virtual-screening hit rates

split.decision: Binding fixed-instance optimization decision (2026-10-29): refit and score all 93 published points (AmpC 36, D4 24, Sigma2 33); train/val/test deliberately overlap; val is a public diagnostic mirror, not a holdout. Each score averages independent fits with literal seeds 0–4. Outer judge seeds 1,2,3 repeat the fixed estimator, changing execution order only. No hidden data or instance seeds exist.

baseline.paper_ref: Published rounded parameters: MSE 0.0013570679439159435; reproduced five-fit mean 0.0013872167540065763.

allowed_changes: the optimizer, parameterization, search strategy, numerical fitting procedure and implementation
surrogate objectives or approximations used internally to find better feasible parameters, while final scoring uses the original MSE and forward model

When retaining the supplied DEAP GA, changing only generations=100, population_size=5000, cxpb=0.4, mutpb=0.4, cxBlend alpha=0.5, mutGaussian sigma=1 or indpb=0.2, or tournament size=3 does not count as a method improvement.
fixed_contract: Fit the fixed bounded six-parameter DOCKMIND statistical model to the93 published observations, minimizing the original target-balanced five-fit MSE.
the bivariate-normal docking-score/affinity model plus Gaussian artifact component and its six published parameter bounds
one parameter vector per target and run, fixed HitRateModel numerical forward map, all93 observations and original definitions
equal weighting of AmpC,D4,Sigma2 and literal fit seeds0..4; fixed-instance in-sample evaluation
Supplied data/splits, evaluation metric, trusted evaluator and lawful information access.

evidence.finding: The interpretable distribution and artifact component are the research model; the six free parameters fit many observations to study scoring accuracy and library composition.
The metric and score rule explicitly require bounded six-parameter HitRateModel reconstruction; the fixed-instance all93-point experiment is an earlier user decision.
The retained trusted numerical map implements the original model independently of candidate code.
